explanation.disagreement_root_cause: 1. Multi-Protocol Dilution: Day 1 and Day 2 CIC-DDoS2019 benign captures contain 37-41% UDP flows (Protocol 17) and ~3% raw IP flows (Protocol 0), for which TCP flag fields (ACK, URG, CWE) are strictly 0. When aggregating across all protocols without conditioning, P(ACK=1) appears as only ~17.3% in Day 1 raw CSVs, 18.9% in the Day 1 train split, and 22.3% in Day 2 test.
explanation.conditioned_tcp_consistency: 2. TCP Agreement across Datasets: When conditioned strictly on Protocol 6 (TCP), the flag frequencies are highly consistent across Day 1 and Day 2: P(ACK=1|TCP) is 29.1% (Day 1 raw), 32.7% (Day 1 train split), and 33.8% (Day 2 test). Similarly, P(URG=1|TCP) is 71.5% (Day 1 raw), 67.6% (Day 1 train), and 66.2% (Day 2 test).
explanation.contrast_with_lab: 3. Lab Environment Homogeneity: In contrast to CIC-DDoS2019's diverse background mix, the isolated lab benign traffic consists exclusively of HTTP/1.1 client browsing and API traffic over TCP (100% Protocol 6). Every data exchange and teardown packet in Linux TCP carries the ACK bit, yielding P(ACK=1) = 1.0000, while URG and CWE are completely absent (0.0000). Thus, the apparent distribution mismatch was exacerbated by protocol mixing in the evaluation tables and by comparing standardized z-score parquet columns without inverse scaling.
